title: India Cracks Down on Fake Paneer as Maharashtra Imposes Statewide Ban
excerpt: From vegetable oil to toilet cleaning acid, adulterated paneer has flooded Indian markets, prompting an unprecedented nationwide enforcement drive and Maharashtra's one-year prohibition on analogue paneer.
body:
• Maharashtra has imposed a one-year statewide ban on the manufacture, storage, and sale of analogue or artificial paneer
  • Over a third of paneer samples tested in Maharashtra between 2025 and 2026 failed quality standards, with 30 declared outright unsafe
  • FSSAI has launched a nationwide crackdown, with raids seizing thousands of kilograms of fake paneer in Hyderabad, Surat, and other cities
  • Adulterated paneer has been found to contain vegetable oil, synthetic milk, starch, and in some cases, toilet cleaning acid
  • The regulator plans to mandate "paneer analogue" labeling, barring non-dairy products from using the word paneer

Maharashtra's Unprecedented Paneer Ban

Maharashtra's Food and Drug Administration has imposed an immediate, statewide ban on the manufacture, storage, distribution, and sale of analogue or artificial paneer for one year. The gazette notification, issued under FDA Commissioner Tukaram Mundhe, covers all districts and explicitly bars hotels, restaurants, caterers, cloud kitchens, and local eateries from using, preparing, or serving synthetic paneer in any dish.

The ban came after alarming test results revealed the scale of the problem. Of 308 paneer and dairy analogue samples analyzed between April 2025 and March 2026, 109 — or 35.4 percent — failed state standards. Seventy-nine samples were sub-standard, and 30 were declared unsafe for consumption. Laboratory testing found natural milk fat frequently substituted with cheap vegetable oils and non-dairy fats.

"Establishments caught stocking or serving analogue cheese as paneer will face severe penalties, confiscation of goods, and legal prosecution under the Food Safety and Standards Act."

— Vikram Pachpute, BJP MLA, Maharashtra

Thousands of Kilograms Seized Nationwide

The Maharashtra ban is part of a broader enforcement wave sweeping across India. In Hyderabad, police seized 825 kilograms of fake paneer made with synthetic milk and vegetable fat. Authorities found traders procuring "cheese analogue" from manufacturers in Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, Maharashtra, and Andhra Pradesh and selling it as genuine paneer.

In Surat, Gujarat, enforcement operations seized 329 kilograms of suspected fake paneer from a single dairy, with investigators finding the operation had been running for nearly two and a half years, selling about 100 kilograms daily. A separate raid in March 2026 netted 1,400 kilograms of fake paneer in the same city. In Ahmedabad, 25 out of 85 paneer samples were found substandard, with penalties exceeding three lakh rupees imposed and action initiated against 12 units.

Toxic Ingredients Raise Alarm

What has particularly alarmed food safety experts is the range of hazardous substances found in adulterated paneer. Beyond vegetable oil and starch, which mimic paneer's appearance and texture, investigations in Punjab uncovered dairies making paneer using toilet cleaner and floor cleaning acid. Food analysts warn these chemicals can severely damage the digestive system, kidneys, and liver.

Fake paneer typically takes several forms: starch or maida mixed with water and chemical thickeners to form solid blocks; cheap milk powder blended with hydrogenated oil and emulsifiers; or, in the most dangerous cases, products containing detergents and synthetic resins. The products are designed to replicate the white, creamy appearance of real paneer while costing a fraction to produce.

FSSAI's National Response

The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India has directed all state food safety commissioners to carry out enforcement measures against paneer adulteration. The intervention came after Union Consumer Affairs Minister Prahlad Joshi wrote to Health Minister J.P. Nadda flagging the "rising trend of sale and use of fake and adulterated paneer all over the country," citing multiple complaints on the National Consumer Helpline portal.

FSSAI is also preparing stricter labeling regulations that would force non-dairy paneer substitutes to be labeled as "paneer analogue" while prohibiting any dairy-related terminology on their packaging. The regulator compared the proposal to existing rules in the frozen dessert market, where only products made with milk fat can be labeled as ice cream.

"These practices amount to consumer deception and pose serious health risks, including food poisoning and allergic reactions."

— Vaibhav Gaikwad Raghunath, Deputy Commissioner of Police, Hyderabad

A Staple Under Threat

The crisis strikes at the heart of Indian vegetarian cuisine. India's domestic paneer market is valued at roughly 65,000 crore rupees, and paneer serves as a primary protein source for millions of vegetarians. Analogue paneer, which substitutes milk fat with vegetable oil, lacks the protein content consumers expect, making the deception both a health and nutritional concern.

Gujarat's Food and Drugs Control Administration has ordered that all food businesses must clearly disclose whether they use milk paneer or analogue paneer on menu cards and notice boards. Over 15,000 food business operators in Ahmedabad alone have been instructed to comply. With Maharashtra's year-long ban now in effect and FSSAI expanding its enforcement drive, the pressure on adulterated paneer networks is likely to intensify in the coming months.
nri_angle: The fake paneer crisis underscores food safety concerns for NRI families visiting India and highlights the importance of sourcing authentic dairy products in diaspora communities.
author: Diaspora Desk
